title: Polarization-preserving wavefront rotator
summary: A K-mirror rotates the wavefront of an incident optical field. However, the rotation always introduces polarization changes in the transmitted field. This is a serious concern for applications ranging from astronomical image derotation to orbital angular momentum spectrum characterization in photonic quantum technology. Recent efforts have shown that the polarization change can be minimized significantly, but these require either a very small base angle that limits the field of view, or mirrors with a customized refractive index.
